generation.scope: A smooth elliptic quartic cannot be the kernel curve of an integral eight-cofactor opposite octic in any four-edge-finite Frobenius candidate. The branch member gives a nontrivial additive torsor and length at most sixteen. For order four the horizontal elliptic double cover and the vertical line multiplicities bound cubic evaluation by eighteen, contradicting twenty, also for nonreduced windows. An integral eight-cofactor kernel must therefore be nodal or cuspidal.

open_mathematics: Treat nodal and cuspidal elliptic kernel curves, then higher cofactor spans, reducible octics, and the general finite-window AS/coverage problem.
